# `sesam edit` reveals one secret to .sesam/tmp, runs $EDITOR on that file, then
# copies the edited content back and seals it.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

exec sesam add secret.txt --group dev
env EDITOR=
env VISUAL=
! exec sesam edit secret.txt
stderr 'neither VISUAL nor EDITOR is set'

exec chmod +x editor.sh
env PATH=$WORK${:}$PATH
env EDITOR=editor.sh

exec sesam edit secret.txt
cmp secret.txt edited.txt
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/secret.txt.sesam
stdout 'edited by editor'
exec sesam verify

exec chmod +x visual-editor.sh
env VISUAL=visual-editor.sh
exec sesam edit secret.txt
cmp secret.txt visual-edited.txt
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/secret.txt.sesam
stdout 'edited by visual editor'
exec sesam verify

exec chmod +x override-editor.sh
exec sesam edit --editor override-editor.sh secret.txt
cmp secret.txt override-edited.txt
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/secret.txt.sesam
stdout 'edited by override editor'
exec sesam verify

# An unsealed edit in the worktree is the starting point, not the object: the
# editor sees it and its own change lands on top.
exec chmod +x append-editor.sh
cp unsealed.txt secret.txt
exec sesam edit --editor append-editor.sh secret.txt
grep 'unsealed edit' secret.txt
grep 'appended by editor' secret.txt
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/secret.txt.sesam
stdout 'unsealed edit'
stdout 'appended by editor'
exec sesam verify

-- secret.txt --
original secret
-- edited.txt --
edited by editor
-- visual-edited.txt --
edited by visual editor
-- override-edited.txt --
edited by override editor
-- editor.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cp edited.txt "$1"
-- visual-editor.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cp visual-edited.txt "$1"
-- unsealed.txt --
unsealed edit
-- override-editor.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cp override-edited.txt "$1"
-- append-editor.sh --
#!/bin/sh
echo 'appended by editor' >> "$1"
